text:
Do not accuse me, I beg you, for the excessive calm

or sadness of my face when I am beside you,

for we look toward opposite places, and one same sun

cannot gild both our brows and hair.


You always look at me without anguish or doubt, as

at a bee enclosed in a crystal urn,

for suffering keeps me in a temple of love,

and for me to spread my wings and fly through the air


would be an impossible failure, if I

wished to try it. But when I look at you, I already see

the end of all love beside the love of now;


beyond memory I already hear forgetting,

like one who, resting on a height, contemplates

beyond the rivers the bitter sea stretched out.

translation.title: Do Not Accuse Me, I Beg You
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the two lovers' unequal perspective and the bitter sea beyond memory.
